To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

heat transfer between a hot tip in ambient air and a substrate is governed by three distinct mechanisms: conduction at solid–solid contact, conduction through the water menisci and conduction through the gas.
the three modes of heat transfer contribute in a similar way to the thermal contact resistance and that they have distinct contact areas ranging from 30 to 1000 nm.

the thermal contact conductances at solid-solid contact, gas conduction, and water meniscus conduction have similar contributions and are of the order of 10 ^{8} W m ^{-2} K ^{-1}, and that the contact radii of the three heat transfer modes differ by two orders of magnitude, ranging from 30 to 1 μ m.
In summary, our research is concerned with
heat transport in nanometer-scale contacts.
the heat transfer mechanisms at solid-solid contact.
the heat transfer between a hot tip (radius ~100 nm) and a solid substrate in ambient air.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heat transfer between the tip and the substrate occurs through the three modes of heat transfer, namely solid-solid, through the water menisci and through the air.
a scanning thermal microscope is a tool to measure the thermal contact resistance of a nanostructure, and the resolution is limited to 1-3μm.

the heat transfer in scanning thermal microscopes is a combination of the heat transfer through the solid-solid contact, the heat transfer through ambient gas, and the heat transfer through water meniscus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the thermal contact conductances between a sharp tip and a substrate are of the order of 10 ^{8} Wm ^{-2} K ^{-1} and that a thermal contact conductance of 10 ^{9} Wm ^ {-2} K ^ {-1} is a practical limit for the thermal resolution of scanning thermal microscopes.
the heat transfer between a hot tip of 100 nm radius and a substrate is governed by conduction at contact, conduction through the water menisci and conduction through the air.
the contact conductance is not a constant and that its value depends on tip geometry and the thermal conductivity of the sample.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat transfer between a tip and a substrate is dominated by the tip-sample thermal contact resistance.
the tip-sample thermal contact conductance is not a single parameter but rather a set of parameters that depend on the tip shape, the substrate surface roughness, and the ambient conditions.
the thermal contact conductances at solid-solid contact and through the water layer are similar, which implies that the thermal contact resistance is mainly due to the water layer.
